text:
sam: @oncall tagging, got a SEV-2 from AcmeCorp — p99 latency for /v1/completions jumped from ~300ms -> ~2.2s starting ~11:45 UTC. Customer key=cust-678, region=us-east-1. They can repro consistently. :rotating_light:
maria: On it. Can you paste the request headers and model version? Any recent rollouts?
sam: headers: Authorization: Bearer key-cust-678; model: redwood-alpha-3b-v2; prompt_length avg=120; max_tokens=512. No staged rollout that I know of, but runtime reported a small kernel upgrade earlier today.
infra-bot: [alert] p95=480ms p99=2.2s on /v1/completions (us-east-1) since 2024-11-07T11:45Z. Error rate unchanged. Top contributor: tail decoding CPU spikes on pods serving redwood-alpha-3b-v2. link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/alert/8234
oliver: Quick triage checklist: 1) isolate by routing a single request 2) check KV cache hit rate 3) look at GPU utilization and host-side queuing 4) consider circuit-breaker throttle for that API key
maria: Running repro now with curl. If we can reproduce, we'll enable per-key rate limit to protect other customers. sam can you run this locally and paste output?
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/completions \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer key-cust-678' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-3b-v2","prompt":"test","max_tokens":64}'
sam: Ran it from us-east-1 - median=340ms, p99=2.15s. Attaching a short trace: trace_id=trc_0a9f1b.
lee: KV cache hit rate for that model dropped to 10% around 11:44 — many cold prefixes. Also host-side CPU spiking on tokenizer thread. GPU utilization steady ~65%. Looks like decoding bottleneck on CPU-bound tokenization + long sequences.
jess: Possible mitigations: - enable emergency fallback to redwood-alpha-3b-q8 for that key - reduce per-request max_tokens to 256 via strict enforcement - enable circuit-breaker at p95 trigger for that key (limit concurrency 8)
oliver: I'll flip a temporary per-key rate limit to 60 req/min and concurrency=8. That should reduce queuing. Also recommend instantly routing that key to the q8 quantized variant if available.
maria: Executing mitigations now: 1) Apply rate-limit policy: `rls apply --key cust-678 --rps 1 --burst 60` 2) Enable concurrency circuit-breaker: `cb set --key cust-678 --concurrency 8 --p95 600` 3) Add model fallback: `route set --key cust-678 --primary redwood-alpha-3b-v2 --fallback redwood-alpha-3b-q8 --policy immediate`
deploy-bot: rollout started -> route-policy/cust-678 (targets: q8 fallback) id=rp_9921.
infra-bot: After rate-limit+fallback: p95 dropped to 410ms, p99 down to 700ms for cust-678. Overall cluster p99 improved to 1.1s.
sam: Customer reports much better response times now, thanks. They want root cause though and a timeline.
lee: Immediate next steps: collect a representative sample of slow requests (trace_id list), correlate with tokenizer CPU stacks, and check if the kernel upgrade changed vectorized tokenizer paths.
jess: I'll open an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml. Suggested labels: p99-regression, model-decoding, customer-escalation. Include repro steps and mitigations applied.
maria: Repro steps for engineers (copy into ticket): 1) Run repro curl (see above) from us-east-1 with key-cust-678 2) Query traces: `select * from traces where trace_id in (trc_0a9f1b, ...)` 3) Check KV cache metrics: grafana panel -> /dashboards/model-cache 4) Check node stacks: `kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/<pod> -- pstack <pid>` 5) Test fallback routing: `route test --key cust-678 --target redwood-alpha-3b-q8`
oliver: Longer-term guardrail items I've put on the backlog: - automatic per-key circuit-breaker when p99 > 1s for 5m - adaptive fallback based on model decoding CPU cost - token budget enforcement on high-cost requests - add canary for kernel patches that touch tokenization
sam: I'll update the customer with the timeline: mitigations applied, perf improved, eng-runtime investigating root cause. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
